newsitem.title: TUNISIA: Tractebel submits offer for Tunisian IPP.
newsitem.headline: Tractebel submits offer for Tunisian IPP.

text.p: Belgian group Tractebel has submitted to the Tunisian government a new offer for the building of the North African country's first privately run power plant, a senior company official said on Tuesday.
Daniel Leroux, Chief Executive Officer of Tractebel, Electricity and Gas International, said he submitted the offer on Monday at a meeting with Tunisian government officials.
"We confirmed to them that we were ready to invest for the long term in Tunisia in the power and gas sector," he told journalists.
"We have submitted a new offer. We plan to use a new technology similar to that we are currently establishing in Chili," Leroux said.
Tractebel is among 10 firms pre-selected last October to compete for winning a tender to build and run Tunisia's first so-called Independent Power Plant (IPP) with an estimated cost of $300 million.
Leroux gave a lower figure, putting the investment at around $150 million. "Our group has enough cash for that investment and we probably will don't need to borrow the money from banks," he added.
"We are integrating power plant and gas with our partnership with SNAM which is able to mobilise gas supply in case the plant would be extended," he said.
SNAM is an Italian natural gas purchaser, transporter and seller and is associated in the gas pipeline from Algeria to Italy through Tunisia.
Energy sources said only eight firms out of 10 are now competing for the final selection with new offers.
Official sources told Reuters that Tunisia's final decision on the winner was expected by the end of the year.

The Independent Power Production (IPP) project is for the development of a combined-cycle gas turbine station which could supply 350-to-500 megawatts of electricity. It is to be located at Rades in southern Tunis.
It will be the first power plant to be privately-run after Tunisia last year scratched the state monopoly on power generation and allowed private investors to run power plants.
The electricity produced is to be supplied to the state-owned Societe Tunisienne de l'Electricite et du Gaz for distribution under a long term contract.
STEG will keep its existing production plants and distribution of electricity by the time being.
